name: Notion
headline: Easy: create a public connection with Any workspace scope and any Notion user can install it. Marketplace listing (5-10 business days) is optional.

firstTest.text: About 5 minutes of clicks once the account has a workspace: New connection, pick OAuth, add a redirect URI, create, then sign in. A brand-new account needs its onboarding finished first, or the Create button stays greyed out with no message.

production.text: Same day. Our OAuth connection was installable in any workspace ('Public') from the moment it was created; no listing or review was needed for our test sign-in. Marketplace listing is optional.

approvalWait.text: None to install a public connection: our test sign-in worked minutes after creating it. Marketplace listing: email response within 5-10 business days, and a Notion security review.

whoCanRegister.text: Any Notion user with a workspace. The New connection form asks only for a name, API token or OAuth, installable-in and redirect URIs; it did not ask for a website, privacy policy or terms. Creating it means agreeing to Notion's Developer Terms.

testMode.text: There is no separate test mode: an OAuth connection is live for any workspace at once. On consent the user picks a workspace and which pages to share (top-level pages are pre-ticked). Our sign-in returned an access token with no stated lifetime and a refresh token.

actions.review: None to install. Marketplace listing needs a security review.

actions.review: None to install. Marketplace listing needs a security review.

actions.review: None to install. Marketplace listing needs a security review.

actions.label: See who the users are
actions.scope: User capability: no user info, or user info without email, or with email
actions.review: None to install. Note: new connections start with 'user info including email' switched on; pick the lowest option you need.

steps.title: Open the developer portal
steps.detail: Profile, Integrations now opens Developer tools, Connections (integrations are now called connections), next to Workers, personal access tokens and MCP tokens.

steps.title: Pick Public and installation scope
steps.detail: Choose OAuth, not API token: an API token is limited to 1 workspace and can't go on the Marketplace. With OAuth, Installable in defaults to Any workspace.

steps.title: Organization fields (not needed to create)
steps.detail: Third-party guides say the form asks for a website, privacy policy, terms and support email. Our form didn't: name, auth method, installable-in and redirect URIs were enough. Expect them for a Marketplace listing instead.

steps.title: Add redirect URIs
steps.detail: OAuth domain & URIs section. Add your callback URI. Notion lists it as required for a public connection.

steps.title: Choose capabilities
steps.detail: After creating, the connection page lists content (read, update, insert, all on by default), comments (off by default) and user info (default: including email). Changes save on their own.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: Configuration tab. Store the secret server-side.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send users to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with owner=user, then exchange the code at /v1/oauth/token with Basic auth. Our exchange returned an access token and a refresh token.

steps.title: Handle the page picker
steps.detail: Users choose pages on the consent screen; top-level pages are pre-ticked and 'People' appears when you ask for user info. Our test shared 3 pages or databases.

steps.title: Optional: list on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Needs Any workspace scope, a listing with name, description, category, tags, images and logo. Notion reviews every submission and replies by email in 5-10 business days.

blockers.title: Created with 'Selected workspaces only'
blockers.fix: Scope can't be changed later. Create a new connection with Any workspace.

blockers.title: Agent sees no pages
blockers.fix: Notion grants access only to pages the user picks in the OAuth page picker. Prompt users to share more pages, or offer a template to duplicate.

blockers.title: Create connection is greyed out
blockers.fix: Happens on a new account with no workspace yet; the form gives no reason. Finish Notion's onboarding to create a workspace, then try again.

blockers.title: Marketplace listing rejected
blockers.fix: Notion emails the reason. Update the listing and resubmit. The connection must be public with Any workspace scope.

blockers.title: Access token stops working
blockers.fix: A refresh flow exists and returns a new access and refresh token. The docs opened here give no lifetimes, so refresh on 401 and save the new pair every time.

agentCan: Write the OAuth flow and token refresh
Choose the minimum capability set from the actions the agent needs
Build the page-picker handling and 'share more pages' prompt
Draft the privacy policy and listing copy
Prepare the Marketplace listing assets list
youDo: Create the connection while signed in to Notion
Publish a privacy policy, terms page and support email
Copy the client secret into your secrets store
Submit the Marketplace listing if you want one
Customers pick the pages to share

drafts.title: Connection description
drafts.body: [Product] connects your AI assistant to the Notion pages you choose. It can read, and when you ask, update or add pages. It never sees pages you don't share.

drafts.title: Marketplace listing blurb
drafts.body: Ask [Product] about your Notion workspace and have it take notes and create pages for you. You pick the pages it can reach. Remove access any time in Notion settings.

drafts.title: Support email auto-reply
drafts.body: Thanks for writing to [Product] support. We reply within [N] business days. If your agent can't see a page, open it in Notion, choose Add connections, and select [Product].

unconfirmed: Answered by our test: the creation form enforced no organization fields (no website, privacy policy, terms or support email). Whether a Marketplace listing asks for them was not tested.
Answered by our test: no review gates a public connection. The Authorization URL was shown as soon as the connection was created, and our sign-in worked minutes later.
Still open: how long tokens live. Our sign-in returned a refresh token but no stated lifetime for the access token, and the docs give no durations.
